findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() may now return null, moving the NPE to callers
findings.body: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the group has been removed concurrently (`modelSupplier.get()` returns null). `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` declares `Long`, and callers are not prepared for a null value: any caller that auto-unboxes the result (e.g. comparisons such as `getSubGroupsCount() > 0`) will throw exactly the NPE this PR is trying to fix, just one frame higher, and REST representations will silently report a missing/null `subGroupCount`. Returning `0L` (or throwing a well-defined model exception that the REST layer maps to 404) would keep the contract non-null and make the behaviour predictable.

findings.title: Other methods using modelSupplier.get() still NPE on concurrently removed groups
findings.body: The same concurrent-removal race fixed in `getSubGroupsCount()` exists unguarded in `getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer)` (line 256), `getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer)` (line 262) and `getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)` (line 268): each dereferences `modelSupplier.get()` directly, which returns `null` when the group row was deleted by another transaction after the cache entry was created. Listing subgroups while a group is being deleted will therefore still produce a NullPointerException / HTTP 500, so the reported issue is only partially fixed.

findings.title: Reader thread is not joined before asserting, so failures can be missed
findings.body: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()` starts a reader thread and asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty immediately after setting `deletedAll` to true. The reader thread may still be inside an in-flight `groups(...)` call at that moment; if that call fails (the exact failure this test is supposed to detect) the exception is appended after the assertion has already passed, making the test silently green. The thread must be joined (with a timeout) before the assertion.

findings.title: Reader thread can spin forever if a group removal throws
findings.body: `deletedAll.set(true)` is only reached if every `groups().group(groupUuid).remove()` succeeds. If any removal throws, the flag is never set and the non-daemon reader thread keeps looping and hammering the admin API indefinitely, which can hang the surviving JVM/test run instead of producing a clean failure. Set the flag in a `finally` block and/or create the thread as a daemon.

findings.title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
findings.body: The 100 groups created in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()` are only removed by the explicit delete loop at the end of the test. If the test fails or an assertion/exception aborts it before the loop completes, the leftover groups stay in the shared `@InjectRealm` realm and can break the other tests in this class (several of which assert on exact group listings/names). Registering each created group with `managedRealm.cleanup()` would make the test self-contained.

findings.title: Shared admin client used concurrently from two threads
findings.body: The reader thread and the main thread both use `managedRealm.admin()`, i.e. the same `Keycloak` admin client instance. The admin client's token manager is not designed for concurrent use; a token refresh happening while both threads issue requests can produce spurious 401/`NotAuthorizedException`s that would be recorded in `caughtExceptions` and fail the test for reasons unrelated to the group NPE, making the test flaky. Use a separate admin client instance per thread.
